headline: Gas Stations Become Epicenters of Hope as Symposium Unveils 'Dream Fuel' Initiative
deck: Local gas stations fill the existential vacuum with motivational posters and dubious bureaucratic procedures.
article:
In a daring move to address the yawning chasm left by the lottery's absence, over 500 attendees flocked to the annual Great Gas Station Hope Symposium this Thursday. Local gas station owners gathered at the Pembroke Community Center, presenting an array of impractical solutions that occasionally grazed the realm of sanity. Each participant was required to present a certified 'Hope Certificate' from the DMV, a bureaucratic hurdle that left many pondering the very essence of hope as they stood in line for two hours.

Among the notable speakers was retired gas station mogul Bill 'Hopeful' Henderson, who unveiled his grand vision for 'Hope Pumps.' These installations, he clarified, would consist of regular gas pumps adorned with motivational posters featuring uplifting quotes like 'Keep Dreaming!' and 'Fuel Your Future!' Each pump will dispense gasoline at a discount of ten cents per gallon, provided customers pay in 'dreams'—a new currency made up of vague aspirations or mere wishes for a brighter tomorrow.

"There’s no better way to fuel your car and your ambition than with our Hope Fuel program! Not only do you fill your tank, but you also fill your heart!" enthused Henderson, blissfully unaware of the disconnect between gas prices and emotional satisfaction. Meanwhile, gas station owner Betty Kratch proposed 'Hope Car Washes' that promise to scrub away existential dread for an additional fee of $5, quipping, "It’s all about clean cars and clear minds!"

As the symposium wrapped up, attendees mingled beneath banners proclaiming, 'Hope is Pumped Here!' while contemplating the lengths they would go for a dash of inspiration in a world where their dreams could only be fueled by unleaded gasoline.
author: Clarence P. Fillmore, Hope Correspondent

oped.title: Gas Stations: The New Shrines of Sappy Sentiments
oped.author: Sir Reginald Pompous III, Chief Hope Engineer of Gasoline Reclamation
oped.body: Ah, fellow inhabitants of the Multiverse, the moment has arrived to revel in the fragrant fumes of hope wafting from our local gas stations! Who needs the lottery, with its chaotic randomness and irritating optimism? We now have the 'Dream Fuel' initiative! Nothing embodies aspiration quite like filling up your tank while contemplating life under a motivational poster that proclaims, 'Fueling Dreams One Gallon at a Time.' I daresay, the real issue here is not the gas prices but the atrocious headwear of the very patrons seeking inspiration! Those floppy hats and fuel-soaked visors are the true dampeners of dreams. Let us banish these horrid fashion choices to restore the sanctity of our fueling stations! Clearly, the only thing more toxic than unleaded is the choice of headgear, and with it, we can revitalize our quest for a brighter tomorrow… even if it comes at the cost of a few dignified outfits.

classifieds.text: Selling my collection of motivational posters featuring inspirational quotes from 2026's most dubious philosophers. Each one carefully laminated and guaranteed to fill your living space with unqualified positivity — or at least distract you from the void!

Seeking Assistant Hope Engineer! Must have experience in revitalizing gas station motivational slogans. Responsibilities include brainstorming uplifting messages while remaining oblivious to the underlying existential dread. Pay in Dream Fuel (subject to approval).

Lost: My will to hope at the local gas station last Tuesday. If found, please return it ASAP, preferably with some Dream Fuel and a motivational playlist. Reward: unlimited access to my best pizza rolls.

Apologies to the gas station attendant for confusing the Dream Fuel initiative with a literal request for gas. I’ll be back to fill up not just my tank but also my spirit—next time, bring extra snacks and a side of optimism!

stories.headline: Local Gas Station Chain Reports Record Sales of 'Hope Cones'
stories.deck: The new flavor features the taste of unfulfilled dreams.
stories.article:
In response to the 'Dream Fuel' initiative, local gas station chain Fill-Up Dreams has launched its latest product: Hope Cones. These ice cream-like cones, infused with the vague essence of aspirations, have seen a staggering 300% increase in sales, according to company spokesperson Larry Tinklebottom, who emphasized that the cones are 'not an actual promise of fulfillment.'

Customers have reported a soothing numbness after indulging in Hope Cones, leading many to suggest that perhaps unstructured hope is best served with sprinkles. However, existentialists have criticized the cones, arguing that the sugary taste fails to capture the bitter aftertaste of reality.

stories.headline: Annual 'Most Hopeless Town' Contest Lures Competitors Nationwide
stories.deck: Applications open now—no hopeful narratives allowed.
stories.article:
This year’s Annual 'Most Hopeless Town' contest has attracted a record number of applicants, with towns from Nebraska to New Jersey vying for the coveted title. Contest organizers noted a significant surge in participation since the 'Dream Fuel' initiative, citing enhanced despair as a driving force for entries.

Hammond, Indiana, last year’s winner, is adopting a new theme of 'Optimism Neutrality' in its bid for a repeat performance. Mayor Stan Frownford declared, 'We’re not just embracing hopelessness; we’re institutionalizing it,' further entrenching Hammond's reputation as the pinnacle of futility in America.

stories.headline: Gas Station Theft of Hope Posters Sparks Nationwide Panic
stories.deck: Suspects may be planning to sell dreams on the black market.
stories.article:
A series of brazen thefts targeting motivational posters from gas stations across the Midwest has left local police forces scrambling for answers. Authorities suspect the culprits are part of an underground movement aiming to monopolize hope, with one officer lamenting, 'These thieves could really stall morale in small towns.'

To combat the rise in motivational poster heists, the Bureau of Bureaucratic Security is deploying additional officers to gas stations, armed with regulations and a distinct lack of enthusiasm. As one beleaguered clerk put it, 'If we can't sell gas for hope, what are we left with? Just fumes and despair.'
